title: Zero Trust Gateways versus Cloud Connectors: who runs what, and where it is available
aliases: is a zero trust gateway a cloud connector

prose.text: A Zero Trust Gateway is a separate deployment type from the Cloud Connector VM that the rest of this area describes.

items.label: GCP.
items.text: {{gcp-managed}} It is likewise Limited Availability: [[cloud-connector.gcp-ztg:limited-availability]]. Creating and operating one: [[cloud-connector.gcp-ztg]].

items.label: Azure.
items.text: {{no-azure-article}} Whether an Azure Zero Trust Gateway can be created is open {{gap:azure-availability}}.

prose.text: {{no-infrastructure}} {{aws-cannot-disable}} The two clouds' pages share the service description but do not establish the same IAM, endpoint, interception, control or API contract {{gap:aws-gcp-parity}}.

Both types appear in the Cloud Connector groups list, distinguished by group type: [[cloud-connector.overview.groups:group-types]]. The Local forwarding method is available to both: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.methods:local-availability]]. Regions where gateways are offered: [[cloud-connector.regions.zero-trust-gateways]].

aws-managed.statement: AWS Zero Trust Gateways are a Zscaler cloud-native service offering in public clouds; they are in Limited Availability and are enabled by contacting Zscaler Support.

quotes: Amazon Web Services (AWS) Zero Trust Gateways are a Zscaler cloud native service offering in public clouds.
AWS gateways are in Limited Availability (LA). To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.

gcp-managed.statement: GCP Zero Trust Gateways are a Zscaler cloud-native service offering in public clouds that is supported in GCP.

quotes: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Zero Trust Gateways are a Zscaler cloud native service offering in public clouds that is supported in GCP.

no-infrastructure.statement: Both the AWS and GCP gateway pages describe securing workloads through the Zscaler Zero Trust Cloud as a SaaS offering without managing security infrastructure, removing the need to deploy NAT gateways, security infrastructure, load balancers and VMs.

quotes: Secure workloads communicating with the internet and private destinations using the Zscaler Zero Trust Cloud as a SaaS offering, without needing to manage any security infrastructure.
Simplify operations by removing the need to deploy NAT gateways, security infrastructure, load balancers, and virtual machines (VMs).

aws-cannot-disable.statement: An AWS gateway's operational status is Enabled or Disabled, but AWS gateways cannot be disabled.

quotes: Operational Status: The operational status of the AWS gateway (i.e., Enabled or Disabled)

no-azure-article.statement: The captured Cloud & Branch Connector help has Zero Trust Gateway articles for AWS and GCP and none for Azure, and the supported-regions article lists only AWS and GCP regions.
no-azure-article.conditions: Absence in the captured help set (vendor/zscaler-help cbc-* captures as of 2026-10-18), not a vendor statement that Azure is unsupported.

aws-endpoint-registration.statement: After an AWS Zero Trust Gateway is added, traffic is routed to it by creating a VPC endpoint of type "Endpoint services that use NLBs and GWLBs" from the gateway's Endpoint Service Name, in a chosen VPC and availability zone, and then pointing route-table entries at that Gateway Load Balancer endpoint.

quotes: After you add an AWS Zero Trust Gateway, you can use the service address to register the endpoint.
Type: Select Endpoint services that use NLBs and GWLBs.
Service name: Paste the Endpoint Service Name from the Zscaler Admin Console and click Verify service.
In the Network settings section, under VPC, from the Select a VPC drop-down menu, select the VPC where you want to deploy the endpoint.
select the Availability Zone where you want to deploy the endpoint
After deploying the endpoint, you must route traffic through it. Traffic passes through the Zero Trust Gateway.
Target: From the drop-down menu, select Gateway Load Balancer Endpoint.

azure-availability.title: Azure Zero Trust Gateway deployment availability
azure-availability.detail: Zscaler's product page positions Zero Trust Gateway for multi-cloud workload traffic and names Azure ExpressRoute among private-connectivity examples, but it does not say in which clouds a gateway can currently be created, its release stage, or entitlement. No first-party per-cloud availability matrix or Azure gateway article is captured.
azure-availability.blocks: saying whether an Azure tenant can use a Zero Trust Gateway instead of Cloud Connector VMs

aws-gcp-parity.title: Whether AWS and GCP Zero Trust Gateways share one operating contract
aws-gcp-parity.detail: Both pages describe a Zscaler-managed cloud-native service with the same benefits list, but the GCP page adds constraints (no DNS interception, Network Security Integration limits) and the AWS page lists endpoint-service columns; identical IAM, endpoint, interception, operational-control and API semantics across the two clouds are not established.
aws-gcp-parity.blocks: reusing an AWS gateway answer for a GCP gateway or the reverse
